scope: Final independent read of all 16 exclusion reasons, evidence/limitations, summary policy/counts and relevant completed primary-source notes. No repeated source search and no public edits.
conclusion: No materially unsupported removal reason or false certificate of national compliance identified. All 16 withdrawals can stand under the stated conservative evidence threshold, with the preserved caveats. Three minor wording/source-scope clarifications are recommended below.
checks: The policy expressly distinguishes insufficient public support from national compliance. Individual exclusion caveats preserve this distinction, including scope-extension, binding-alternative and national-only-reporting cases.

No withdrawal relies only on absence of an injured person, fine, refusal, patient or affected operator. Those observations are ancillary; operative reasons concern permitted protective variation, missing proof of incompatible scope extension, intelligible reporting categories or plausible binding alternative duties.

The 16 exclusion IDs and reason strings exactly match the summary withdrawn records. Current public data count52, 46leads/6findings, 21countries/27EUchanges matches summary counts. This is a consistency check, not a repeat of browser verification.

The remaining differences across retained and withdrawn cases have stated substantive grounds: noise Portugal has an advance marketing condition, Austria specific repeal rationale and a remaining Commission chain, Finland a remaining Commission chain; Hungary/Latvia retain only national reporting with incompatibility unresolved. Dutch SLAPP has distinct restrictive jurisdiction conditions plus specific judicial disagreement; Irish/Polish withdrawals preserve credible but unproved non-equivalence arguments.
